neighbours.label: ' down' in a non-literal phrasal verb: bearing down, biting down, dampen down, water down; walking or sitting down stays quiet
fire: When bearing down on a deadline, stay calm.
She chipped a tooth from biting down on an olive pit.
The council tried to dampen down the protests.
He hunkered down for the long winter.
The heat died down after the storm.
They want to water down the bill.
Stop bogging down the team with reports.
Try to calm down the crowd.
quiet: When waiting on a deadline, stay calm.
She chipped a tooth from a fall on the ice.
The council tried to understand the protests.
He walked down the long road.
The heat rose after the storm.
They want to read the bill.
He went down the stairs with the reports.

notes: Probes: 'He sat down' 0.04, 'We walked down' 0.02, against 0.42-0.65 for the phrasal uses. Corpus max is small (4.28). Other top tokens (' together', ' Southern') are not covered.
